steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Normative social influence (NSI): conforming to be accepted and avoid rejection - leads to compliance. Driven by the desire for social approval. | Key Fact: Informational social influence (ISI): conforming because we believe the group is correct - leads to internalisation. Most likely in ambiguous or novel situations. | Key Fact: Agentic State theory (Milgram): people obey because they enter an 'agentic state' - they see themselves as instruments carrying out another's wishes, not responsible for their actions. Binding factors (politeness, fear of disruption) keep people in the agentic state. | Key Fact: Legitimacy of authority: we obey people we perceive as having legitimate power (uniform, institutional context). When authority is perceived as illegitimate, obedience decreases

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between normative and informational social influence. | Describe Milgram's agentic state theory and evaluate its usefulness for understanding obedience. | Explain how minority influence can lead to social change.
